title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the first section ('Ensembles à quatre éléments') of a 'Fourbis combinatoires' preliminary to Grothendieck's notes on moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2. The claims, in modern terms:

(1) Any 4-element set I carries a canonical structure of affine plane over F_2. The structure is given intrinsically by a subgroup V ⊂ S_I, namely the Klein four-group of double transpositions together with the identity. V ≅ F_2^2, but not canonically, and V acts simply transitively on I, so I is a V-torsor.

(2) Characterisation of V. It is the unique nontrivial abelian normal subgroup of S_I; the normal subgroups of S_4 are 1, V, A_4 and S_4, and A_4 is not abelian. V is also its own centraliser, so S_I/V acts faithfully on V by conjugation. In fact S_I/V ≅ Aut_gr(V) = GL(V) ≅ GL_2(F_2) ≅ S_J, where J is the 3-element set of nonzero elements of V* (equivalently of V, or the projective line P(V)). This gives the exact sequence 1 → V → S_I → S_J → 1. It is identified with the affine-group sequence 1 → V (translations) → Aut_aff(I) → Aut_{F_2}(V) → 1, using that every permutation of a 4-element set is affine.

(3) Combinatorial dictionary. The three elements of J correspond to:
- the three partitions of I of type (2,2);
- the three fixed-point-free involutions of I (margin note), i.e. the nonzero translations;
- the three vector lines in V (or V*), each of which defines an equivalence relation on I whose quotient is an affine line.

The six 2-element subsets of I are the six affine lines of the plane I. The map P_2(I) → P_{2,2}(I), A ↦ {A, I∖A}, sends an affine line to its direction. The fibres have 2 elements: the two parallel lines in a given direction.

The next page goes on to the equivalence Aff_2(F_2) ≃ Ens_4 and to the completeness of S_4 (trivial centre, all automorphisms inner). The latter is proved by recovering I as the set of four Sylow 3-subgroups.

Purpose. In the elliptic-curve setting the four Weierstrass points of E (the branch points of x: E → P^1) form exactly such a 4-element set, a torsor under E[2] ≅ F_2^2. The quotient S_4 → S_3 is the anharmonic group acting on the Legendre λ / cross-ratio. These combinatorics (and the Z/4 version announced on the previous page) are the bookkeeping for level-2 and level-4 structures.
errors: Notational slip: J = V* should be the set of nonzero elements of V* (or P(V*)), not V* itself; V* has 4 elements.
'≠ {0}' uses additive notation for a subgroup of S_I (harmless).
The final identification of P_2(I) → P_{2,2}(I) with the direction map is stated only on the next page; the page itself breaks off mid-sentence.

ideas.what: Canonical F_2-affine plane structure on any 4-element set via the Klein four-group V ⊂ S_4 acting simply transitively
ideas.modern_name: S_4 ≅ AGL_2(F_2); Klein Vierergruppe as translation subgroup

ideas.what: Exact sequence 1 → V → S_4 → S_3 → 1, identified with translations → Aut_aff → GL_2(F_2); V is the unique nontrivial abelian normal subgroup and is self-centralising
ideas.modern_name: S_4/V_4 ≅ GL_2(F_2) ≅ S_3 (resolvent cubic / anharmonic group)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Lagrange's resolvent, Galois theory of quartics)

ideas.what: Dictionary between (2,2)-partitions, fixed-point-free involutions, directions/lines, and the map from 2-subsets (affine lines) to their directions
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorics of AG(2,2); parallel classes of the affine plane of order 2

deep.surprise_reason: Entirely classical group theory and finite geometry, presented in Grothendieck's characteristic intrinsic/functorial style as a preliminary for level structures on elliptic curves. Nothing new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: Left margin note is more plausibly 'ou aussi aux trois involutions sans points fixes', i.e. the three double transpositions, rather than 'trois ensembles de partitions sans points fixes'.
Line 2: the crossed-out words read like 'torseur affine sur', replaced by 'd'espace affine' written above.
'Le sous-groupe V ⊂ S_I est le seul sous-groupe distingué abélien ≠ {0}': the word crossed out before 'il est son propre' is illegible; 'centralisateur' is written over a struck word.
Near the end, the word above the struck-out text after 'aux 6' looks like 'bipartitions' or 'classes'; uncertain.
The symbol for the symmetric group is rendered 𝔖 / 𝔊 inconsistently across pages; it is the same symbol S_I.
